svg.title: Deciding the sign of an atom exactly
svg.desc: An eight-row count table whose unique-S1 atom is exactly zero, shown as a product of local ratios, and three ways to decide the sign.

g.font-family: 'Source Sans Pro', 'Source Sans 3', 'Latin Modern Math', 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif
g.text: DECIDING THE SIGN OF AN ATOM EXACTLY
(b) The unique-S1 atom is a product in disguise
The other two supported states have local ratio 1. Weighting by rows,
This interval also contains nonzero values.
pid-rs exact-sign audit: binary S1, S2, T; 12,869 nonempty count tables with n ≤ 8, 308,856 coordinates.
Sixteen nontrivial cancellation coordinates were found, all at n = 8. Each coordinate is (1/n) log R, R ∈ ℚ>0.
